essence: Body declared god's temple, self the eternal god: worship with I-am-He feeling after casting ignorance.
Breath-bodied Gaṇapati first-worshipped: saluted by all beings, bestowing wished boons.
Vaṭuka apāna-named, worshipped by adepts: remover of the humble folk's pain and doubt.
Sadguru's mind-strength makes the universe shine Śiva-pathed: attention itself the gift.
Sense-goddesses feast the heart-lotus: consciousness-made bliss-Bhairava at the core.
Bhairavī's ceaseless world-play of dawning and digesting: reflection-formed, ever praised.
Brāhmī intellect-formed offers resolve-flowers from the lord's petal: perception confirmed.
Śāmbhavī mother offers I-flowers from fire's petal: ego itself the oblation.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta with bhakti (wonder held in devotion)
rasa.sthayibhava: vismaya with rati (wonder with loving attachment)
rasa.justification: The body disclosed as temple seating gods in every faculty: wonder at the ordinary made divine, carried by the repeated I-praise. Desire-to-praise, not to know, drives each beholding.

sections.SUMMARY: Body named temple, self named eternal god: ignorance swept off, worship in I-am-He feeling. Breath-bodied Gaṇapati first, saluted by all, giving wished boons. Vaṭuka apāna-named, adepts at his feet, lifting humble pain and doubt. The true guru spotless, whose mind-strength shines the world Śiva-pathed. Sense-goddesses feasting the heart-lotus for consciousness-made bliss-Bhairava. Bhairavī reflection-formed, dawning and digesting the world unceasing. Brāhmī intellect-formed offering resolve-flowers from the lord's petal. Śāmbhavī mother offering I-flowers from fire's petal.
sections.FUNCTION: Sets body as temple, posts breath as gatekeepers, gives attention as the guru's gift, seats bliss at the core, and starts the flower-offerings.
sections.KEY TERMS: deho devālayaḥ (body-as-temple — the ground of the whole round); so'ham (I-am-He feeling as worship-mode); prāṇa/apāna (outgoing/ingoing breaths as gatekeepers); avadhāna (attention as the guru's gift); cinmaya (made of consciousness); vimarśa (reflection as her form); kusuma (flowers as sense-offerings); ahaṅkṛti (I-making as act, not thing).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Gatekeepers honored and the presiding pair enthroned, perception and ego lead the directional round.
sections.BOUNDARY: All giving here is praise; nothing is demanded.
sections.EXPLANATION: The body turns from dwelling to temple and the self from tenant to god, with one act of sweeping and one feeling of identity. Then the doors: prāṇa and apāna as Gaṇapati and Vaṭuka, worshipped first because breath holds the house together. The guru gives the only instrument that matters — attention — by which the world shines walkable toward Śiva. At the center sits bliss, consciousness-made, fed by the senses themselves; beside him reflection, digesting the world she dawns. The circle starts dealing its flowers: resolve from intellect in the east, I-ness from ego in the southeast fire.
